genxml.title: VIA/IC Ensemble ICE1724 (Envy24HT) PCI audio controller registers

struct.name: CCS_CONTROL
struct.doc: Bit 7 is a soft reset of the whole chip. The public driver writes 1, waits, then writes 0; the datasheet does not say whether the bit self-clears. Bits 6 to 0 are reserved.

struct.name: CCS_IRQ_MASK
struct.doc: Interrupt mask. A set bit masks the source. The datasheet states this polarity only for MT03; here it is inferred from the reset value and the driver's use. Every source is masked at reset.

struct.name: CCS_IRQ_STATUS
struct.doc: Bits 7 and 5 are write-1-to-clear. Bit 4 is read only and clears when its source in the multi-channel register clears. Bits are sticky.

struct.name: CCS_SYSTEM_CONFIG
struct.doc: The public driver copies EEPROM bytes 6 to 9 here; the datasheet says the driver loads them, and hardware does not. The reset value means 24.576 MHz, no UART, no inputs and four stereo DACs.

struct.name: CCS_AC97_CONFIG
struct.doc: Converter type and AC'97 slot layout. Bit 7 reflects the power-up strap on GPIO 0 in reverse and may be overwritten.

struct.name: CCS_I2S_FEATURES
struct.doc: Converter capabilities, written from the EEPROM.

struct.name: CCS_SPDIF_CONFIG
struct.doc: S/PDIF transmitter enable and capability bits. Bit 6 is read only and reflects the SPDTX pin during reset, reversed: 0 means the transmitter is on the board.

struct.name: CCS_UART_TX_COUNT
struct.doc: Valid bytes in the MPU-401 transmit FIFO, which is 32 deep.

struct.name: CCS_UART_RX_COUNT
struct.doc: Valid bytes in the MPU-401 receive FIFO, which is 32 deep.

struct.name: CCS_MIDI_DATA
struct.doc: MPU-401 data port.

struct.name: CCS_MIDI_COMMAND
struct.doc: MPU-401 command and status. The datasheet gives no bit definitions. The public Linux driver's reading (bit 0 UART mode, bits 1 to 4 FIFO empty and full flags) is an expectation, not established.

struct.name: CCS_UART_SETTING
struct.doc: MPU-401 watermark. Both watermarks reset to 0.

struct.name: CCS_I2C_DEVICE
struct.doc: Writing this register starts an I2C transfer, so the busy bit must be clear first. Device address 1010000 is reserved for the configuration EEPROM.

struct.name: CCS_I2C_BYTE
struct.doc: I2C byte address.

struct.name: CCS_I2C_DATA
struct.doc: I2C data byte, written before a write transfer and read after a read transfer.

struct.name: CCS_I2C_STATUS
struct.doc: Bit 7 mirrors the EEPROM strap on GPIO 3 at reset, so a board with an EEPROM reads 80. The printed reset 00 conflicts with that text; the text is taken. Bit 0 is busy. Bit 1 is reserved, keep 0.

struct.name: CCS_GPIO_DATA
struct.doc: GPIO data, bits 15 to 0. A bit takes a write only while its write-mask bit is 0. Bits 22 to 16 are in ccs_gpio_data_hi.

struct.name: CCS_GPIO_MASK
struct.doc: GPIO write mask, bits 15 to 0. Reset masks every bit, so no GPIO data can be written until software clears mask bits. Bits 22 to 16 are in ccs_gpio_mask_hi.

struct.name: CCS_GPIO_DIRECTION
struct.doc: GPIO direction in three bytes, 0x18 to 0x1A. Bits 22 to 0 are defined: 0 is input, 1 is output. Bit 3 doubles as the EEPROM strap at reset; bit 2 is forced to input while the test-enable pin is active.

struct.name: CCS_POWER_DOWN
struct.doc: Each bit set stops or powers down the named clock. Bits 6 and 1 are reserved. The ALSA driver writes 0 here, which is an expectation.

struct.name: CCS_GPIO_DATA_HI
struct.doc: GPIO data, bits 22 to 16 in bits 6 to 0. Masked by ccs_gpio_mask_hi.

struct.name: CCS_GPIO_MASK_HI
struct.doc: GPIO write mask, bits 22 to 16 in bits 6 to 0.

struct.name: MT_IRQ_STATUS
struct.doc: One bit per source; write 1 to clear. The multi-channel source bit in the controller's status register is inferred to be the OR of the unmasked bits here. Bit 3 is set by any underrun or overrun flag.

struct.name: MT_SAMPLING_RATE
struct.doc: Sample rate. When bit 4 is 1 the rate code is ignored and the S/PDIF input clock is the master, with the master clock on the SPMCLKIN pin.

struct.name: MT_I2S_FORMAT
struct.doc: Clock ratio and data format. Bit 3 selects a 128x master clock; 176.4 kHz forces it. Bit 2 is listed read-write with no description.

struct.name: MT_IRQ_MASK
struct.doc: Source mask, same bit layout as mt_irq_status. A set bit masks the source. Every source is masked at reset.

struct.name: MT_AC97_INDEX
struct.doc: AC'97 register index. Valid only in AC-link mode, though the drivers also use the converter reset bit in I2S mode.

struct.name: MT_AC97_COMMAND
struct.doc: AC'97 command and status. The datasheet limits this register to AC-link mode. In I2S mode bit 7 is inferred to reset the converters, from the sibling part's datasheet and both drivers.

struct.name: MT_AC97_DATA
struct.doc: AC'97 data port.

struct.name: MT_PDMAI_ADDRESS
struct.doc: Start of the interleaved playback buffer. Bits 1 and 0 read 0, so the address is dword aligned. The datasheet says the field is in dword units; the drivers store the byte address unshifted, which is taken here.

struct.name: MT_PDMAI_COUNT
struct.doc: Buffer size in dwords less one, counting down as data moves. Reloads at zero, so the buffer wraps. Bits 18 to 0 are used.

struct.name: MT_DMA_START
struct.doc: Read-modify-write only. A 1 starts the stream and a 0 stops it. Bit 3 is read only, 0. Bit positions are the same as mt_irq_status.

struct.name: MT_PDMAI_STREAMS
struct.doc: Interleaved channel count; see enum interleave. Sets which of PDMA1 to PDMA3 are free.

struct.name: MT_DMA_UNDERRUN
struct.doc: Underrun on playback or overrun on record, per stream. Bit positions are the same as mt_dma_start. Write 1 to clear; any flag raises the interrupt through mt_irq_status bit 3.

struct.name: MT_DMA_PAUSE
struct.doc: Pause and resume, per stream; bit positions are the same as mt_dma_start. A 1 pauses and a 0 resumes.

struct.name: MT_PDMAI_TERMINAL
struct.doc: Interrupt interval in dwords less one. Counts down; at zero it raises the stream's source. Write only. The index line says 1C to 1D, but the layout covers 1C to 1E, which holds the 19-bit field.

struct.name: MT_RDMA0_ADDRESS
struct.doc: Start of the first record buffer. Dword aligned, same encoding as mt_pdmai_address.

struct.name: MT_RDMA0_COUNT
struct.doc: Buffer size in dwords less one, counting down. Read the position only after at least two sample frames have passed.

struct.name: MT_RDMA0_TERMINAL
struct.doc: Interrupt interval in dwords less one. Write only.

struct.name: MT_ROUTING
struct.doc: Source of each output channel, in I2S mode only, adding at most one sample time of delay. The layout is established; the zero reset is inferred from the printed 00h for a 32-bit register.

struct.name: MT_RDMA1_ADDRESS
struct.doc: Start of the second record buffer. Dword aligned, same encoding as mt_pdmai_address.

struct.name: MT_RDMA1_COUNT
struct.doc: Buffer size in dwords less one, counting down.

struct.name: MT_RDMA1_TERMINAL
struct.doc: Interrupt interval in dwords less one. Write only.

struct.name: MT_SPDIF_CONTROL
struct.doc: S/PDIF transmitter channel status. Reads 0000 when the SPDTX pin is floating or high, and 2000 at power-up when the transmitter is fitted. Every field except validity is writable only while ccs_spdif_config bit 7 is 0.

struct.name: MT_PEAK_INDEX
struct.doc: Stream to meter. 0 to 7 are the eight interleaved slots, 8 and 9 the S/PDIF left and right, 10 and 11 RDMA0, 18 and 19 RDMA1. Other values are ignored.

struct.name: MT_PEAK_DATA
struct.doc: Peak level of the selected stream, the nine most significant bits of the level. Reading clears the peak.

struct.name: MT_PDMA_ADDRESS
struct.doc: Start of the playback buffer for the S/PDIF stream and the three extra stereo pairs. Element 0 is PDMA4 (S/PDIF), 1 is PDMA3, 2 is PDMA2, 3 is PDMA1. Dword aligned.

struct.name: MT_PDMA_COUNT
struct.doc: Buffer size in dwords less one, counting down. Element order as mt_pdma_address.

struct.name: MT_PDMA_TERMINAL
struct.doc: Interrupt interval in dwords less one. Write only. Element order as mt_pdma_address.

struct.name: PCI_VENDOR_ID
struct.doc: PCI vendor ID, IC Ensemble.

struct.name: PCI_DEVICE_ID
struct.doc: PCI device ID. The same ID is used by the VT1720 (Envy24PT), so it does not tell the parts apart.

struct.name: PCI_COMMAND
struct.doc: Bit 1 (memory space) and bits 3 to 7 and 9 are hardwired to 0. The datasheet lists bit 8 as read-write but describes it as hardwired to 0; it reads 0 here.

struct.name: PCI_STATUS
struct.doc: Bits 15 to 12 are write-1-to-clear. Bit 11 is hardwired to 0. Bit 14 reads 0. Bit 4 (capability list) is hardwired to 1.

struct.name: PCI_REVISION
struct.doc: Vendor revision. The datasheet shows it as a placeholder; the value is not given.

struct.name: PCI_CLASS
struct.doc: Class code: multimedia, audio. The field is 24 bits in the header; the programming interface byte at offset 0x09 reads 0.

struct.name: PCI_CACHE_LINE
struct.doc: Not supported; reads 0.

struct.name: PCI_LATENCY_TIMER
struct.doc: Writes take effect in eight-clock steps: writing FF reads back F8.

struct.name: PCI_HEADER_TYPE
struct.doc: Type 0, single function.

struct.name: PCI_BIST
struct.doc: Built-in self test is not supported.

struct.name: PCI_BAR0
struct.doc: Controller registers (CCS), 32 bytes of I/O space. Bits 31 to 5 are the base.

struct.name: PCI_BAR1
struct.doc: Multi-channel registers (MT), 128 bytes of I/O space. Bits 31 to 7 are the base.

struct.name: PCI_SUBSYSTEM
struct.doc: Subsystem IDs. Loaded from the EEPROM after reset when one answers, otherwise the reset value. Writable only while the subsystem mask bit is set. Which EEPROM bytes map to which half is not documented.

struct.name: PCI_EXPANSION_ROM
struct.doc: Reserved; the part has no option ROM.

struct.name: PCI_CAPABILITY_PTR
struct.doc: Points to the power-management capability at 0x80.

struct.name: PCI_INTERRUPT_LINE
struct.doc: Set by firmware. FF means the interrupt is not routed.

struct.name: PCI_INTERRUPT_PIN
struct.doc: INTA#.

struct.name: PCI_GRANT_LATENCY
struct.doc: Minimum grant in the low byte, maximum latency in the high byte. Both 0.

struct.name: PCI_SVID_MASK
struct.doc: The table places the subsystem ID mask at 0x40 and the register section at 0x42. Bit 7 is the control that makes the subsystem IDs writable. The offset is taken from the register section.

struct.name: PCI_PM_CAPABILITY_ID
struct.doc: Capability ID: power management.

struct.name: PCI_PM_NEXT
struct.doc: End of the capability list.

struct.name: PCI_PM_CAPS
struct.doc: Power management version 1.0. D2 is supported, D1 and PME are not.

struct.name: PCI_PM_CONTROL
struct.doc: Power state select.

struct.name: PCI_PM_DATA
struct.doc: Power management bridge extension and data. Read only, reset 0.
